title: bug: worktree-mode sh/ps1 twin drift in labels and diagnostics (recovery-checkpoint status, interrupted-gate CheckRun, hooked-commit reason, post-flight MOE_WORKTREE_MOE_PRESENT)
description:
Filed by WT-19's whole-epic adversarial review (task-b1ca54f2716442be889a14623eb59983, step 7).

PROBLEM. There are four small sh/ps1 drifts in worktree mode, and parity-check's string families cannot see them. Each changes only a label, a diagnostic or an evidence row. None moves a branch, and none records a false pass.
(a) On a fresh claim, sh labels a recovery checkpoint status=UNKNOWN.
(b) ps1 records no infra-failure CheckRun for an interrupted worktree-mode gate.
(c) sh misreports why a hooked commit's sparse helper failed.
(d) No landing post-flight prints MOE_WORKTREE_MOE_PRESENT, which design §1.6 requires.

EVIDENCE. Checked on merged tree 88e507e5, which is moe/work-2026-10-24 at 1558f141 plus the WT-19 task.
(a) scripts/moe-agent.sh:10512 calls worktree_preflight with "${RESUME_TASK_STATUS:-}", which is empty unless the session is a resume. So sh:7868 sets LAND_STATUS="${3:-UNKNOWN}". scripts/moe-agent.ps1:9789-9791 passes the preflight context's task.status instead.
(b) The sh EXIT trap (sh:269) calls finish_gate_observation (sh:5890-5897), which records any gate that started but was never recorded as infra-failure. ps1 does that only in the shared landing's finally (ps1:6216-6230). In worktree mode:
- Invoke-MoeWorktreeCompletion's catch/finally (ps1:7264-7271) only warns and releases the lease;
- the outer finally (ps1:11188) only stops the gate child.
(c) The sh hooked-commit worktree arm empties private_git when sparse-checkout or read-tree fails (sh:5484-5487). The signing-config comparison then runs with GIT_DIR='' and writes 'hooked-commit-config-mismatch' (sh:5514-5515). ps1 throws 'hooked-commit-worktree-failed' (ps1:5048-5050).
(d) docs/plans/2026-10-30-per-task-worktrees.md:69 says "A post-flight that finds it still lands ... and prints the code". The only emitters are:
- pre-flight: sh:3439, ps1:3317;
- removal: sh:8199 and :8248, ps1:7726 and :7782;
- the sweep: sh:8405, ps1:7931.

IMPACT.
(a) The same recovery gets a different commit subject and ledger status on each engine.
(b) On Windows the ledger loses the interrupted gate attempt. No landing happens, but the rail-1 audit gets harder.
(c) An operator chases a signing mismatch that does not exist.
(d) A W that grew .moe is reported only at the next pre-flight.

FIX DIRECTION. Mirror whichever twin is right:
(a) sh passes the preflight context's task status.
(b) ps1 records the infra-failure CheckRun in the worktree completion's finally, or in the outer finally, when MoeGate.Started is set and MoeGate.Recorded is not.
(c) sh writes 'hooked-commit-worktree-failed' and returns when the sparse helper fails.
(d) Both landing post-flights check W/.moe, print MOE_WORKTREE_MOE_PRESENT, and still land, as §1.6 says.
definitionOfDone: On a fresh claim, sh labels a worktree recovery checkpoint with the task's real status, as ps1 does.
ps1 records an infra-failure CheckRun for an interrupted worktree-mode gate on the exit paths sh's finish_gate_observation covers.
When the hooked-commit sparse-checkout/read-tree helper fails, both twins report 'hooked-commit-worktree-failed'.
Both landing post-flights print MOE_WORKTREE_MOE_PRESENT when W/.moe exists and still land, per design §1.6.
parity-check.sh/.ps1, worktree-landing.sh/.ps1 and postflight-safe (bash and powershell) all pass.

implementationPlan.description:
Drift (a), sh only: the worktree recovery checkpoint's status label on a fresh claim. Test first, then fix.

Today the main-loop line `if [ "${MOE_WT_MODE:-}" = worktree ]; then worktree_preflight "$PREFLIGHT_TASK_ID" "$PREFLIGHT_TASK_TITLE" "${RESUME_TASK_STATUS:-}"; fi` (about scripts/moe-agent.sh:10540) passes RESUME_TASK_STATUS. That variable is empty unless this is a resume, so worktree_preflight sets LAND_STATUS="${3:-UNKNOWN}" and the recovery reads status=UNKNOWN. ps1 passes the pre-flight get_context's task.status instead ($moeWtStatus at the Invoke-MoeWorktreePreflight call, about ps1:9823-9825).

TEST (scripts/tests/postflight-worktree.cjs, wtRecover, about :741). After the existing `/ recovered\n$/` subject assertion, add two assertions on run wt-recover-2's recovery commit m[2]. That run is a fresh claim, and the fake's get_context answers status WORKING.
- `git log -1 --format=%s m[2]` contains `[status=WORKING `.
- `ledger(p).filter(x=>x.sha===m[2]).map(x=>x.status)` deep-equals ['WORKING'].
Add a one-line comment naming task-d2d6ac4b (a). Run `MOE_WORKTREE_ONLY=wt-recover` on both engines, using the two targeted legs of step 5's command with C=wt-recover (mem:gotcha-postflight-worktree-mutant-copy has the WSL-to-Windows details). sh must FAIL with an AssertionError showing UNKNOWN (RED). ps1 must pass.

FIX (sh only, at that call site). Read the status from PREFLIGHT_CONTEXT with the same stdin python pattern that worktree_preflight already uses for its commits read: `json.load(sys.stdin)["task"]["status"]`, printed only when it is a str, else "" (also "" on any exception). Store it in a global MOE_WT_PREFLIGHT_STATUS, because the main loop is not a function and cannot use `local`. Pass it as the 3rd argument. Comment: `Twin: $moeWtStatus, the pre-flight get_context's task.status; RESUME_TASK_STATUS is empty on a fresh claim.`

worktree_preflight itself stays unchanged; its `${3:-UNKNOWN}` still covers a missing status.

Why this is safe:
- provision_worktree stops the seat with MOE_WORKTREE_CONTEXT_FAILED unless get_context answered for this task, so in worktree mode the context is always present.
- PREFLIGHT_CONTEXT is fetched for fresh claims and resumes alike (about sh:9922), so a resume also gets its real status, exactly as ps1 does.
- In worktree mode, teardown_rescue returns before it reads LAND_STATUS, and every post-flight path sets LAND_STATUS itself. Only the recovery label changes.
- Shared mode (preflight_landing) is untouched.

Error handling: a failed or empty parse leaves the value empty, and the label falls back to UNKNOWN as before. It never aborts the pre-flight.

After the fix: `bash -n scripts/moe-agent.sh`, then re-run wt-recover on sh and ps1. Both must pass (GREEN). Edit tracked files only with the Edit tool (global rail). In the task worktree, edit the wrapper in place.

implementationPlan.description:
Drift (c), sh only: the reason a hooked commit gives when its worktree helper fails. Test first, then fix.

Today, in moe_commit_with_hooks' worktree arm (6th argument `worktree`, about scripts/moe-agent.sh:5507-5516), a failure in the stdin sparse-checkout, the `read-tree -mu`, or the post-read .moe check only sets private_git="". The signing-config comparison then runs with GIT_DIR='', so git reads no repository config, and it writes 'hooked-commit-config-mismatch'. ps1 New-MoeHookedCommit throws 'hooked-commit-worktree-failed' there (about ps1:5080-5085), and its finally removes the scratch.

TEST. Start ONE new block of cases directly after `async function wtLeaseSignal(){...}`. That function ends just before the `// A function of this wrapper, by name` comment (about :1048). Head the block with a comment naming task-d2d6ac4b. This step adds `async function wtHooksSparse()`:
- p=repo('wt-hooks-sparse',{settings:{...LANDS,commitHooks:true}}).
- A .git/hooks/pre-commit (mode 755) that only writes a marker file under root, as wtHooks does.
- landRun(p,'wt-hooks-sparse-0',{'src/a.txt':'task\n'}): a checkpoint that provisions W with no stub. Then t=revOf(p.top,p.branch) and main=mainOf(p).
- r=landRun(p,'wt-hooks-sparse',{},{...REVIEW,WT_GIT_FAIL:'sparse-checkout'}). A reused W runs no sparse-checkout at pre-flight on either twin (only an added or half-made W does), and no qualityGate is set. So the hook helper's sparse step is the only call the stub fails.
- One assert.deepEqual with tail(r.log), expecting:
  - mainOf(p)===main;
  - the last done(p) row's [outcome, code, message.trim()] is ['failed','MOE_COMMIT_FAILED','the completion commit was refused: hooked-commit-worktree-failed'];
  - the `MOE_RESCUE_REF ... reason=commit-failed` sha is t;
  - the marker is absent;
  - `git worktree list --porcelain` lists exactly 2 worktrees.

Registration: add ONE new statement line directly after the existing `Object.assign(cases,{'resume-unread':...});` line (about :1677): `Object.assign(cases,{'wt-hooks-sparse':wtHooksSparse});`. Steps 3 and 4 extend this same line. Never edit the existing long registration lines or the completion and lease cases: task-f9874361 edits this suite next to them, and adjacent-line hunks conflict at the worktree landing (mem:gotcha-adjacent-line-edits-conflict-in-worktree-landing). Assert the wrapper's own reason, never the stub's stderr (mem:gotcha-postflight-worktree-git-stub).

Run `MOE_WORKTREE_ONLY=wt-hooks-sparse`. sh must FAIL (RED: config-mismatch); ps1 must pass.

FIX (sh, worktree arm only):
- Change the arm's condition to `[ "${6:-}" = worktree ]`.
- Fail it on `[ -z "$private_git" ] || ! { <the existing stdin sparse-checkout && read-tree> } > "$err" 2>&1 || [ -e "$scratch/.moe" ] || [ -L "$scratch/.moe" ]`. ps1 throws the same reason when `rev-parse --absolute-git-dir` fails.
- The failure branch writes 'hooked-commit-worktree-failed' to "$err". It then runs the same `git -C "$MOE_TOP" worktree remove --force "$scratch"` the function ends with; if that removal fails, it writes the existing 'Could not remove the private hook worktree; refusing publication.' instead. Then `return 1`.
- Keep the stdin patterns and their MSYS comment exactly as they are (mem:gotcha-git-bash-stub-path-and-msys-sparse).
- The shared-mode path (no 6th argument) must stay byte-identical (rail 4).

Error handling: HOOK_COMMIT_SHA stays empty and nothing is committed. The caller's existing route in wt_land_rounds is unchanged: LAND_MESSAGE 'the completion commit was refused: <last 2 lines of err>', then a commit-failed rescue ref and a failed row.

After the fix: `bash -n`, then re-run wt-hooks-sparse on sh and ps1 (both GREEN). Then run `node --test scripts/tests/hook-isolation-bash.test.mjs`, which slices moe_commit_with_hooks out of the wrapper; all 9 tests must pass, as they do on the target today. Indent every new line: a bare `}` at column 0 inside the function would break that slicer.

implementationPlan.description:
Adversarial self-review of this task's own diff, using the adversarial-self-review skill.

Scope and placement:
- `git diff` touches exactly scripts/moe-agent.sh, scripts/moe-agent.ps1 and scripts/tests/postflight-worktree.cjs.
- moe-agent.ps1 keeps its UTF-8 BOM; `bash -n` and the PS 5.1 ParseFile are both clean.
- Each fix stays local to its own site, per the governor's placement note:
  - (a): only the main-loop worktree_preflight call;
  - (c): only the worktree arm of moe_commit_with_hooks; the shared-mode path is byte-identical;
  - (b): only Invoke-MoeWorktreeRounds' gate block; Invoke-MoeLanding, Invoke-MoeFrozenGate, Invoke-MoeWorktreeCompletion and the outer finally are unchanged;

- In the suite, no existing case, helper or registration line changed except wtRecover's two new assertions. The three new cases sit in one block after wtLeaseSignal and are registered on one new line after the 'resume-unread' line.

Edge cases:
- Twice or concurrently: the (b) finally runs once per round, and Recorded=$true makes a second pass a no-op. A passed gate is already Recorded and removed, so a round-2 finally never records round 1's gate.
- A Ctrl+C during the record itself: the outer finally still stops the child and removes the workspace.
- Null or empty inputs: an empty PREFLIGHT_CONTEXT or status gives UNKNOWN, as before; an empty W path skips (d); an empty private_git takes (c)'s worktree failure branch.
- Windows: (d)'s Get-Item -Force sees a dangling junction. On ps1, the (b) test interrupts only the wrapper's console.

Evidence and regression:
- Each new assertion was RED on the engine that had the drift and GREEN after its fix. Copy the RED AssertionError lines from steps 1-4 into the completion summary.
- `node --test scripts/tests/hook-isolation-bash.test.mjs` still passes 9/9.
- Merge risk: re-check task-f9874361's hunks (`git diff $(git merge-base <its moe/task branch> <target>) <its branch>`) against yours. If any hunk is adjacent to yours, say so in the completion summary (mem:gotcha-adjacent-line-edits-conflict-in-worktree-landing).

If the review changes any tracked byte, re-run step 5's exact command and use that output as the evidence.

executionContract.intendedBehavior:
Four sh/ps1 twin drifts in worktree mode are closed, each at its own site:
(a) On a fresh claim, sh labels a worktree recovery checkpoint (its commit subject and its record_commit status) with the pre-flight get_context task.status, as ps1 does.
(b) For a worktree-mode gate interrupted after it started and before its record (a Ctrl+C, or a throw), ps1 records exactly one infra-failure CheckRun against that round's frozen candidate, as sh's finish_gate_observation does.
(c) When the hooked-commit worktree helper's setup fails (no private gitdir, sparse-checkout, read-tree, or .moe present), sh reports 'hooked-commit-worktree-failed' and removes its scratch worktree, as ps1 does.
(d) Both worktree worker post-flights print MOE_WORKTREE_MOE_PRESENT when W/.moe exists and still land unchanged (design §1.6).
acceptanceCriteria: DoD 1: wtRecover's fresh-claim recovery commit subject contains '[status=WORKING ', and its record_commit row has status WORKING, on both engines (RED on the target's sh, GREEN after the fix).

DoD 2: wt-gate-interrupt records exactly one record_check_run, [infra-failure, the record_candidate id, M = merge-tree(main,T)], before the single lease release and the deregister. main does not move, T keeps the bytes, and there is exactly one finalize, 'failed'. This holds on both engines (RED on the target's ps1).

DoD 3: in wt-hooks-sparse, the failed completion row's message is 'the completion commit was refused: hooked-commit-worktree-failed' on both engines. A commit-failed rescue ref holds T, no hook ran, and no scratch worktree is left (RED on the target's sh).

DoD 4: in wt-moe-post, each of the checkpoint and completion runs prints exactly one '[WARN] MOE_WORKTREE_MOE_PRESENT:' line and still lands only src/a.txt. W/.moe stays on disk (RED on the target, both engines).
DoD 5: the step-5 command exits 0. That means parity-check.sh/.ps1, the targeted sh/ps1 runs (4 ok each), worktree-landing.sh/.ps1, and postflight-safe bash and powershell with failureClass NONE.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
(b) placement. The description offers Invoke-MoeWorktreeCompletion's finally or the outer finally. Both need the frozen candidate, which is a local of Invoke-MoeWorktreeRounds; $script:MoeFrozen is null in worktree mode, so Send-MoeCheckRun would carry a null candidate, and the fake and the daemon would refuse it. Plumbing it through $L would also work, but then on the throw path the record comes after the unlanded route's finalize. A try/finally around the gate call inside Rounds keeps the candidate in scope, records first on every path, keeps the lease release after it (as sh does), and stays out of Invoke-MoeWorktreeCompletion, which task-f9874361 edits.
(a) A fix inside worktree_preflight was rejected: the call site mirrors ps1's $moeWtStatus one-to-one and leaves the function contract alone.
(c) Besides the sparse/read-tree/.moe failures, the arm also fails on an empty private_git, because ps1 throws the same reason when rev-parse fails; shared mode is untouched.
(d) The check sits at the head of the post-flight with a sentence that is true even when autoCommit is off, rather than being duplicated in ps1's separate completion and checkpoint branches.
I did not add parity-check literals: the behavioural cases pin every drift on both engines, and the DoD does not ask for them.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: The postflight-worktree.cjs suite runs every case on both engines; postflight.sh and postflight.ps1 run it in full, so postflight-safe covers the new cases. launch() opts.ready gives sh a SIGTERM and ps1 a real console Ctrl+C (consoleSupervisor). The ps1 gate child is CREATE_NO_WINDOW, so only the wrapper sees the Ctrl+C, and the shared interrupt-int scenario already proves that a ps1 finally can send the CheckRun during a pipeline stop. WT_GIT_FAIL fails any git call with that exact argv element. A reused W skips provisioning's sparse-checkout and read-tree on both twins, so WT_GIT_FAIL=sparse-checkout with no qualityGate hits only the hook helper. The fixture repo sets a local user.name, so sh's GIT_DIR='' comparison reports config-mismatch today. hook-isolation-bash.test.mjs slices moe_commit_with_hooks up to the first '\n}\n'; it is green on the target (9/9).
